Southington BKMB · Sub Sale

Sub Sale Playbook

Everything from opening a season to a kid taking an order at a doorstep — the four flows, in the order they happen, with a slot for every screenshot and a shot list for the training video.

Phase 1Start the season Phase 2Kids sign up Phase 3Drivers sign up Phase 4Taking an order Phase 5 · ReceiptPhase 6 · DrivingAppendixScreenshot list AppendixVideo plan
Phase 1

Start the season

Subsales chair

Once a year, before anybody signs up. It lives in Subsales → Settings → Set Up Season — the last tab along the top. That page shows the current season and a Set Up Season button; the button opens a wizard with eight numbered steps you can move through with Next, or jump around using the numbers at the top. Nothing is lost if you close it — it always shows what's set up right now, so it doubles as a mid‑season check.

Addresses aren't part of this The address book looks after itself — it goes out to the seller app on its own, and anything it can't place waits in Settings → Address Management → Needs Review, which you can work whenever. It used to be a step in here and it isn't any more.
Get the roster first Before you open the wizard, use Download the seller sheet on that page (or or a blank one for an empty template) and email it to the band director. Name, phone and email, one per line. Having it in hand means you won't have to stop half way through step 3.
  1. →

    Getting there

    Subsales → Settings, then the Set Up Season tab. You'll see the current season, when setup was last run and by whom, the roster download, and the blue Set Up Season button that opens the wizard.

    SS-01 The Set Up Season tab, with the seller-sheet download and the Set Up Season button.

  2. 1

    Start the season

    Type a name under Name for this season — e.g. 2026-2027 — and press Start this season. If you already started it, skip straight to step 2.

    Starting a season keeps every old record. It retires last year's teams and files everything from now on under the new name. Only do this once a year.

    SS-02 Step 1 with the season name box and Start this season button.

  3. 2

    Sales days

    Pick every day the kids are going out. Enter a Sale day, optionally a second date after through to add a whole range at once, then Add. Each day appears in the list below with a Remove link.

    A day with sign-ups can't be removed here That's deliberate — pulling a date out from under kids who already signed up for it would orphan their sign-ups.

    SS-03 The sale-day range picker with dates listed below it.

  4. 3

    Sellers

    Sellers carry over year to year, so this is a check of who's coming back rather than a fresh list. The banner tells you how many are on the roster.

    Coming back this year lists everyone with their phone number, and flags anyone with no email. Untick whoever has left — nobody is ever deleted, they're marked inactive so last year's orders and reports still show their name. Tick all and Untick all are there for a big clear-out.

    Then add this year's new people, either way:

    • Paste into the box — name, phone, email, one per line. Copy columns straight out of a spreadsheet; tabs work as well as commas, and a header row is ignored.
    • Upload the sheet the band director sent back — Excel .xlsx or .csv.

    Press Check this to see what will happen before anything is saved.

    Matching is by phone number Someone already on the list is updated rather than duplicated — so this is also how you backfill email addresses onto people who don't have one. Someone whose number changed comes in as a new person.

    SS-04 Step 3 showing the roster banner and the "Coming back this year" tick list.

    SS-05 The paste box, the file upload, and the Check this button.

  5. 4

    Pricing

    The items and prices sellers see when they take an order. The banner tells you how many are showing in the app.

    Edit a name or price straight in the table. Remove deletes a row, Add product adds one, and Save Products commits it. Ten slots, no more.

    Remove what you aren't selling this year. Every order keeps its own copy of the item name and the price it sold at, so deleting a product here doesn't reach back into last year's orders, reports or delivery manifests — they still print Turkey and the price the customer actually paid. With only ten slots, leaving retired items in place is what costs you.

    Visible is for a pause, not a retirement Untick it for something you've run out of mid-season and expect to bring back — it disappears from the seller app without losing its row. For an item that's gone for good, remove it and free the slot.

    SS-06 Step 4 with the product table, Add product and Save Products.

  6. 5

    Sales mode

    Two radio buttons, then Save this choice:

    • Teams — kids go out together on a sale day and the team's orders are tallied together.
    • Individual — each kid sells on their own and their own orders are tallied to them.

    This is what decides which login the app asks for in Phase 4, so it's worth getting right before the kids install anything.

    SS-07 Step 5 with Teams selected.

  7. 6

    Admin contact

    One field: the subsales admin phone number. The chair changes year to year, so it's set per season.

    The step shows you exactly where it lands, so you can check it before saving:

    • The text receipt a customer gets — the full message, with its character count and how many SMS segments that costs.
    • What a seller sees on a card-paid order — a card-paid order can't be edited by a kid, so the app tells them to have the customer call this number.

    SS-08 Step 6 with the number entered and both previews showing.

  8. 7

    Open sales

    The master switch: tick Sellers can take orders and press Save. The banner tells you whether sales are currently open or closed.

    With it off, nobody can take an order in the app — which is what you want between sale days and once the fundraiser is over.

    Leave this off until the kids have signed up Turning it on is the last thing you do, not the first.

    SS-09 Step 7 showing sales OPEN.

Phase 2

Kids sign up

Students

Each student says who they are, picks their team, and ticks the days they'll sell. Send them to /signup/ — no password, no account, about a minute. The three tabs across the top are 1. Your Info, 2. Team, 3. Dates. Teams are the kids' own business — they group themselves, and the first one to sign up creates the team the others then join.

  1. 1

    Your information

    Name and phone number. They should pick their name from the list as it appears — that's the roster you loaded in Phase 1 recognising them. Typing a fresh name creates a new person instead of matching the one already there.

    The phone number is checked against the roster before they can go on, and it's also what they log into the seller app with, so a typo here costs them twice.

    Wrong number? They get "Phone number does not match our records for this user" and an Email Us link to the subsales chair. That usually means the roster has an old number — fix it in Phase 1 step 3 rather than having them sign up as somebody new.

    SS-10 Step 1 with a name being picked from the roster autocomplete.

  2. 2

    Team

    Now that it knows who they are, this step opens with Current Sign-ups — everything they've already signed up for. A kid coming back to add a date can see what they've got rather than guessing.

    Under Sign Up for Another Date they type their team name. Matching teams appear as they type — tap one to join it. If nobody has made the team yet, typing the whole name creates it.

    One kid creates the team, the rest join it The kids sort out their own teams — this isn't something an adult assigns. The tidy way to run it: whoever is organising the team signs up first and types the name. The team exists the moment they press Next – Select Dates, so everybody else can pick it off the list straight away, without waiting for the first kid to finish. One person types the name; nobody else has to spell it the same way.
    Why it matters The delivery run is divided per team, per sale day. "Team 1", "team one" and "Team One" created by three different kids are three different teams, and their orders get split three ways on delivery day. Typing a name that already exists does join the existing team — but only if it's typed the same, so picking from the list is the safe move.

    SS-11 Step 2 showing current sign-ups and the team search.

  3. 3

    Dates

    Tick every day they can sell, then Complete Signup. These are the sale days from Phase 1 step 2 — if a date is missing, it was never added there.

    They can come back any time to add more days; it will show what they already have rather than starting over.

    SS-12 The date chips, with several picked.

  4. →

    Changing something later

    Coming back to /signup/ and getting through step 1 shows every date they've signed up for, across every team, with a Details button on each one.

    A row marked (Driver Missing) has nobody driving that day yet. That's the thing to chase — a sale day without a driver doesn't happen.

    Details opens that one day and lets them:

    • See who else is on the team that day
    • Name their driver, which is the same job the parent does in Phase 3 — either side can fill it in
    • Switch to a different team, or remove the registration if they can't make it
    Dropping out matters The delivery for a sale day is split between the kids signed up for it. Somebody who quietly doesn't turn up still has orders assigned to them. Removing the registration is a thirty-second job that saves an argument on delivery day.

    SS-13 The Details window: team members, the driver box, and the advanced actions.

Changing a sign-up later. The same link handles it: typing their name shows what they already have. Dates they are signed up for are filtered out of the picker, so a child cannot un-tick a day they want to drop — they have to use Remove This Registration against that day. It is the most common thing a parent will ring about. Change team is there too.
Phase 3

Drivers sign up

Parents

Parents aren't in the student roster, so they register themselves at /driver-signup/. A driver is attached to the team and days their child is already signed up for — which is why the child has to sign up first.

  1. 1

    Find your child

    Child's name (autocompletes) and their phone number, then Find My Child's Team. That looks up which team and which days the child signed up for.

    If nothing is found The child hasn't signed up yet, or the phone number doesn't match what they used. Have them do Phase 2 first.

    SS-14 The lookup when the child hasn't signed up yet — the most common thing to go wrong.

  2. 2

    Which days will you drive?

    Every day their child is signed up for is listed, grouped by team, and they all start ticked — uncheck any days you are not driving. A child on two teams shows both, so a parent covering only one team's days unticks the other.

    Their own name and phone number go at the bottom of the same screen.

    SS-15 The day picker, grouped by team, with the driver’s own details underneath.

  3. 3

    Register as driver

    Register as Driver confirms it. The You're all set! screen lists back every team and date they're now driving, which is worth a glance before they close the tab.

    Drivers don't get a share of the orders They're the designated driver for the days they signed up for. When the delivery list is split between kids, drivers are left out of that split on purpose — they're still required for the delivery itself.

    SS-16 The confirmation, listing every team and date they are driving.

Phase 4

Taking an order

Students · at the door

This is the part the kids need to know cold, and the part the video covers. The app lives at /portal/. It works with no signal — orders are saved on the phone and sent up when the signal comes back — so a spinning bar is not a reason to type the order twice.

  1. 1

    Install it once, before the sale day

    Open /portal/ and use Install App when it offers. On iPhone that shows the Share → Add to Home Screen steps; on Android it installs directly.

    It still works in the browser if they say no — orders are cached either way. What installing protects is the queue: an iPhone clears a website's saved data after about a week of not opening it, and an order taken with no signal lives in that storage until it syncs. On the home screen that clear-out doesn't apply.

    SS-17 The offer appears above the login. Install Now on Android installs it; on iPhone it shows the Share → Add to Home Screen steps.

    SS-18 Tapping Not Now says what it costs. The offer comes back in a week.

  2. 2

    Log in

    Which login they see depends on step 5 of the season setup:

    • Team selling — team name and access code.
    • Individual selling — full name, phone number, and pick your team.

    They stay logged in. They should not have to do this at every door.

    SS-19 Name, phone and team. This is the login for individual selling; team selling asks for a team name and access code instead.

  3. 3

    Say yes to location

    The phone asks once: "subsales.southingtonbkmb.com Would Like to Use Your Location". Tap Allow. That's what lets Use my location fill the address in from where they're standing.

    It only asks once Tap Don't Allow and the phone will not ask again. The button goes red and reads Location off. Nothing else breaks — they can still type addresses all day — but the shortcut is gone until it's turned back on.

    There are two ways back, both below. The first stays inside Safari and only affects this site — use that one. The second goes through Settings and turns location on for every website, so it's the fallback, not the default. On Android it's the padlock at the left of the address bar. Tapping the red Location off button in the app spells this out on screen too.

    SS-20 The prompt, as it appears the first time. Allow.

    The quick way, without leaving Safari

    SS-21 Page Menu → Website Settings for subsales.southingtonbkmb.com → set Location to Allow. This one is for this site only.

    If that isn't there, go through Settings

    SS-22 Open Settings and search for Safari.

    SS-23 Under Settings for Websites, tap Location.

    SS-24 Choose Allow. Note the heading: this one covers all websites, not just ours.

    4. 📍 Use my location. Beside the address box. It fills in the nearest address in the offline address book to where the phone is standing — useful on a long driveway or an unmarked house. Two things to tell the kids: it picks the closest address it knows, which can be next door, so the house number always needs checking; and if it reads Location off the phone has not granted permission, which is what SS-20 to SS-24 cover. Typing the address by hand works exactly the same.

    Known limit: there is no maximum distance on that match. Out of range of the loaded ZIP data, or on poor GPS, it will still fill in whatever is nearest rather than saying it cannot tell.
  4. 5

    Who's buying

    • Customer name
    • Address — start typing the house number and street; it fills in from the address book. Use my Location fills it in from where they're standing.
    • Unit / Floor / Apt — only if there is one.
    • Phone number — used for delivery.
    Pick the address from the list A typed-in address that isn't in the book has to be chased down by hand later. Picking the suggestion means the driver gets a real map location.

    SS-25 The order screen as it opens. Everything for one order is on this page.

    SS-26 Type the house number and the street appears. Note the dot at the top right is amber — this is working with no signal, from the address book downloaded at login.

  5. 4

    What they're buying

    Use + and − on each item. The total updates as they go. There's a donation box for someone who wants to give without buying a sub.

    SS-27 Two Turkey, two Combo and a $5 donation — the total keeps itself up to date.

  6. 6

    How they're paying

    Three buttons — Check, Cash, Digital. Tap one; it lights up. Only one can be selected.

    • Check — a box appears for the check number. It's the short number in the top right corner of the check, usually three or four digits. Not the long line of digits along the bottom — that's the bank's account number, and it's the thing people type by mistake.
    • Cash — nothing else to fill in.
    • Digital — a QR code appears over the screen for the customer to scan. It only appears once the customer and address are filled in.

    SS-28 Tap one and it fills in. Check adds a box for the number.

    SS-29 Cash asks for nothing else — the selection is the whole job.

    SS-30 The check number is the short number in the top right corner — not the long line along the bottom.

    SS-31 Turn the phone round and let them scan. The countdown is the life of the link, and Back out to Cash/Check is always there.

  7. 7

    Save it, then move on

    Save the order and walk to the next house. If there's no signal it goes in the queue — Queued Orders in the header shows how many are waiting, and Sync now sends them once there's a signal.

    My orders shows what they've taken so far.

    Never enter the same order twice If they aren't sure it saved, check My orders or Queued Orders first. A double entry means a double delivery and a wrong total.

    SS-32 Every saved order reads back what was agreed: the items, the donation, the total and how they paid — with the check number when there is one. This is the screen to read aloud before walking away. Edit is right there if it is wrong.

    SS-33 My orders with no signal. The order is there under Local (pending sync) and will send itself. The panel says it cannot check the server rather than pretending there is nothing there — so an empty list is never a reason to type the order again.

    SS-34 The same panel back in signal. Local (pending sync) is empty because the orders moved across on their own — nobody pressed anything. That is what the queue is for.

    SS-35 The end-of-day tally, and the number the seller hands money against. Subs and donations are listed separately, added once, and the payment methods sit underneath as the breakdown of how that total arrived — not more lines to add up. It matches the Orders screen for the same seller and day, figure for figure.

Phase 5

The customer's receipt

Automatic · then the chair

Everything so far ends when the order is saved. This is what happens next, without anybody doing anything: the customer gets a text, and that text is the start of a conversation that stays attached to their order.

  1. 1

    The text goes out on its own

    If the customer ticked Text me about this sub order, a receipt is queued the moment the order reaches the server and sent within about thirty seconds. Nobody sends it. Nobody can forget to send it.

    It is deliberately short — a link, not a list:

    Southington BKMB got your order. Receipt: https://s.southingtonbkmb.com/…
    Save this number so our texts reach you. Reply STOP to opt out.

    A text is charged per 160 characters. Spelling out every item made it two texts, and more as orders got bigger. A link is the same length whether they bought one sub or twenty.

    No tick, no text. If the box was not ticked the order still goes through exactly the same — there is just no receipt and no conversation. That is the customer's choice and the law's.
    SS-36

    The receipt text as it arrives on a phone. Include the whole bubble and the sender number.

    ss-36-receipt-text.png

  2. 2

    They tap the link

    The link opens their order: what they bought, the total, where it is going, and how they paid. It works for months, so they can check it the morning of delivery.

    It does not name the student who took the order. It is a public web address, and a child's name does not belong on one.

    SS-37

    The receipt page, opened from the text. Whole page, phone width.

    ss-37-receipt-page.png

  3. 3

    They reply, and it reaches somebody

    Every reply lands in Subsales → Text Messages, filed against that customer's order. One row per person, whoever has waited longest at the top, with a red count for anything unanswered.

    The count also shows in the black bar at the top of every admin page, so a reply gets noticed without anyone going looking for it.

    SS-38

    Text Messages, the conversation list, with at least one unread.

    ss-38-conversations.png

  4. 4

    Answer with the order in front of you

    Open the conversation and the order sits beside it — items, address, delivery notes, and what has already been changed. Reply from the box underneath and it goes back as a text.

    Edit this order opens the same editor as the Orders screen, right there, so a change and the message asking for it never get separated.

    Tell customers to save the number. Phones increasingly file texts from unknown numbers away in a separate list. A customer who has saved the number, or replied a few times, stops being unknown. Worth a sentence at the door: “save that number, we’ll text you about delivery.”
    SS-39

    A conversation open: messages on the left, order panel on the right, reply box underneath.

    ss-39-conversation.png

Phase 6

Driving on a sale day

Parent driver

Phase 3 got the driver signed up. This is the day itself: what they see, what money they are responsible for, and how it gets handed over. A driver is carrying other people’s cash around a neighbourhood — the app’s job is to make the number they owe unarguable.

  1. 1

    Sign in exactly like a seller

    Same app, same address, same login — phone number, then pick the team. There is no separate driver app and no separate password.

    The app works out that they are driving for that team on that day from their sign-up, and shows them the driver view instead of the order form.

    Driving is per team, per season. Somebody who drives for one team is an ordinary seller everywhere else, and driving last season does not carry into this one. If a driver sees the order form instead of the money screen, their sign-up for that team and date is what to check.

    SS-41 The same login screen a seller sees — there is nothing driver-specific about it. What changes is what appears after logging in: a driver gets the money screen, a seller gets the order form.

  2. 2

    Money Accountability

    One number in a green block: what they should be holding. Underneath, where it came from — cash, checks with a count, and digital marked already paid, nothing to collect.

    Digital is shown but deliberately not included in the total. That is the same trap the end-of-day tally used to fall into: money that has already reached the bank is not money in somebody’s pocket, and adding it makes an honest driver look short.

    Below that, the team’s totals for the day and a line per seller, so a driver collecting from four kids can tick them off.

    Read it as: cash + checks = hand this in. In the shot, $70 cash and $80 in one check make $150. The $135 of card payments is listed for completeness and is not part of the $150.

    SS-40 The driver’s money screen. The big number is what should be in their hands right now — cash plus checks, nothing else. Refresh pulls in orders the kids have synced since they last looked, and Updated just now says how current it is.

  3. 3

    See what a seller has collected

    Tap a seller’s name and their orders open underneath — every one they have taken, with the time, how it was paid, what was bought and the total. Their two figures are on the row itself: what they are holding, and what they have sold.

    Work down it as they hand money over. If a kid’s phone still has orders queued they will not be here yet — get them to tap Sync now where there is signal, then Refresh.

    A mismatch is a question, not an accusation. Nine times in ten it is an unsynced order, or a check counted as cash. Check Queued orders on the kid’s phone before anything else.

    SS-42 Tapping a seller’s name opens every order they have taken that day — time, how it was paid, the items, any donation, and the total. This is the list to check money against, order by order.

  4. 4

    Fix an order if it is wrong

    Every order in that list has an Edit button. Use it when a kid has typed the wrong thing — a sub miscounted, a check entered as cash, an address that will not find the house.

    The edit opens the ordinary order form with EDIT MODE across it. Change what is wrong and save; it syncs like any other order.

    An order paid by card cannot have its items changed. The customer’s card was charged at the door for exactly that order, so what they bought is fixed — the app will not let a seller or a driver change it, and neither will the server. Delivery notes and the address stay editable. If a card order is genuinely wrong, an administrator has to void and refund it.
    Every edit is recorded. The order’s history shows what changed, when, who did it, and whether they were the seller, the driver or an admin. Nobody has to remember who fixed what.
    SS-44

    An order open in EDIT MODE from the driver’s screen, showing the Cancel edit button. Capture this after v3.66.1 — earlier shots show the address suggestions open over an address that was already filled in, and no way out of the edit.

    ss-44-driver-edit.png

Appendix B

Video plan

For students

One video, about three minutes, screen-recorded on a phone with a voice-over. Cover only Phase 4 — signing up is a one-off they'll do with a parent, but taking an order is the thing they do forty times in an afternoon.

0:00–0:15

Open on the doorstep

Phone in hand, front door in shot. No screen yet.

"You're going to take orders on your phone. It works even when you have no bars — here's the whole thing."

0:15–0:35

Install and log in

Tap the icon on the home screen, show the login, show it going straight in.

"Install it the night before. You log in once — not at every house."

0:35–1:15

Name and address

Type a house number slowly. Let the suggestions appear. Tap one. Then show Use my Location.

"Type the house number and pick the address from the list. Picking it from the list is what gets the driver to the right door."

1:15–1:45

Adding the subs

Tap + a few times on two items. Show the total moving.

"Plus and minus for each kind. Watch the total — read it back to them before you take the money."

1:45–2:25

Getting paid

Tap each payment button so the highlight moves. Show the check-number box. Show the QR overlay and closing it.

"Check, cash or digital — tap one. For a check, write the number in. For digital, turn the phone around and let them scan it."

2:25–2:50

Save, and no signal

Save the order. Then put the phone in airplane mode, take another order, and show it landing in Queued Orders.

"No bars is fine. It saves on your phone and sends itself when you're back in signal. Don't type it again."

2:50–3:00

The one rule

Back to My orders, scroll the list.

"If you're not sure it saved, check My Orders first. Never enter the same order twice."

Record it in a test season with sales switched off Everything on screen should be made up. Nothing in the video should be a real customer, and no order recorded during filming should end up on a real sale day.

Sub Sale Playbook · Southington BKMB. Screenshot slots are numbered SS-01 to SS-23 and match Appendix A. Phase 1 is once a year; phases 2 and 3 are once per person; phase 4 is every single door.
